newsitem.title: ITALY: Gianni Versace comes home for last time.
newsitem.headline: Gianni Versace comes home for last time.

text.p: The ashes of slain fashion designer Gianni Versace returned home to Italy on Friday ahead of a private family funeral near the peaceful home on Lake Como he loved so much.

Reporters at the stylist's residence in the lakeside village of Moltrasio saw two black limousines carrying Versace's sister Donatella and brother Santo sweep through the gates and disappear down the drive soon after they arrived from Miami.

A private plane carrying the family and an urn containing the ashes of the designer, who was shot dead on the steps of his Miami Beach mansion on Tuesday, landed in the nearby town of Bergamo to avoid crowds of waiting media in Milan.
A helicopter then whisked them to Como where the jet-setting designer had an 18th century neo-classical villa he used as a retreat from the racy world of international glamour.

Versace counted Princess Diana, Princess Caroline of Monaco, pop stars Madonna and Elton John and a host of other stars of stage and screen as his favourite clients, but his final homecoming was a strictly private affair.
His family was expected to hold a service near the three-storey villa during the weekend.
Reporters saw two private security guards at the village cemetery, where the family has expressed a wish for Versace to be laid to rest, and the chapel was being cleaned.
A memorial mass was planned in the enormous Roman Catholic cathedral in Milan, Italy's fashion capital, early next week.
Versace, 50, was shot dead in broad daylight on Tuesday on his way back from buying the morning papers.
Police have mounted a massive manhunt for Andrew Cunanan, a 27-year-old homosexual prostitute and alleged serial killer whom they describe as their only suspect in the murder.

Santo, the business brains behind Versace's worldwide fashion empire, and Donatella, creator of the company's Versus line and a talented designer in her own right, have vowed to carry on where their brother left off.
They have appealed to the media to respect their privacy and paramilitary Carabinieri police were patrolling Lake Como in a motor launch to keep prying eyes at bay.
Versace, famed for his ritzy glamour showered on the rich and famous, had been coming to Lake Como for around 10 years to escape the stresses of life in the fashion fast lane.

His aristocratic, three-storey villa was situated in a part of Italy that has become a playground of the rich and famous. But shutters and a thickly wooded, walled garden with cobbled paths and statues offered tranquility.
Versace, hailed as one of the kings of fashion, was born in the poor southern city of Reggio Calabria where he learnt the basics of his trade from his seamstress mother.

He launched his first collection under his own name at the age of 31 and developed a reputation for brash, sexy clothes, often in shimmering metallic fabrics stolen from the aerospace industry but nevertheless beautifully cut and crafted.
In partnership with his brother and sister, he attached the Versace name to haute couture, jeans, T-shirts, perfumes and even bedlinen and home furnishings.
Total revenue from all brands was 1.705 trillion lire ($975 million) in 1996. ($1=1,748)
